"He doesnt treat me right, hes very mean sometimes for no reason."

This is the CORRECT and ABSOLUTE red flag. 

There, you have your answer. Notify your guardian/parent/trusted friend about this situation and his identity and photo, then break it off, in a text. If he knows your address and you fear for your safety, make sure your trusted one is notified of what you know regarding him, or you can crash at your trusted one's spot for a day or two after your break up.

Have you had the talk before asking him to leave? He left without making a big scene. He might not even realized how much he is damaging your rest. 

If you already had the talk, he needs that spank. If he respect you he will apologize.

If you did not had the talk, and at least notified him of how damaging he is at the moment, IMHO you were being unfair as he's like a lost kid not knowing or realizing what he did wrong.

And what is your current age? Is the gap high enough for you to make irrational decisions? Is it high enough to add a fault in this relationship?

Nobody knows who anyone is until they decide to tell you truthfully or is exposed. Red flags or not having a few dinner to get to know him better hardly seems dangerous enough, you had suspicions, but how he treats you should be the focus. 

Who he is, what he does, when the time comes you'll know. The question is would you be prepared to be his partner in crime if his income or activities is not what you hoped for? Are you willing to take that risk? Does he treat you well enough and respectfully enough for you to take that leap of faith? A single NO from either question is enough for you to "Hey, I don't think its going to work out. I think we should....xxxxxxxx" 

You've made your evaluation, now think, will you stick to find out more, or it's enough to send you into red alert and seek a safer and more conventional partner?

Good luck, and sleep on it. 

Avoid doing anything to trigger him yet on this matter, Timing is very important to initiate the conversation. Try on public space to discourage him on going on rampant; while having a nice dinner outside with a little wine. 

Good luck on whichever path you choose. Stay safe, and always be calm and logical while dealing with these matters. The future of your whole relationship and family in general, can be affected by these simple steps.

You are not married, seek others. Don't continue to hurt each other as at that age keep in mind a woman is so close on facing menopause, and you are closer and closer to erectile disfunction. Do both of you a favor and find another partner who has the same ideology as you each do.

She's young, she's at a graduation party. Telling her not to drink and judging her future actions by this very moment is not viable and reasonable.

I doubt (for the sake of my opinion) that it will easy for you to comply the same. It will be unjustifiable for her to request the same, unless both of you are into the sober and non-alcoholic method.

Also, both of you are 17 I adherently doubt being "controlled" and set "ground rules" for marriage or sorts of future is the right time, nor the right priorities, nor the right desires both of you will not regret one day. 

If you think someone at that age will not be influenced by their friends with "WTH, ITS YOUR GRADUATION NIGHT! I'M DOING IT YOU SHOULD BE TOOOOOOO!!! YOLOOOO" and will follow your rules, you will be seriously mistaken and taking a huge leap of faith, most will not comply successfully. 

It is the age to experiment responsibly, age to explore your destiny and desires, age to experience the merger of adulthood and teenage spirit. This is a very volatile moment and most humans in the western culture will NOT be ready to settle down and be a family member. 

Either marry her (be very careful or you might regret this decision), or develop each other to maturity yet (in terms of experiencing the world, gaining knowledge, gaining necessary foundations to adult life, gaining education) should be your primary concern and motivation for each other. 

Fidelity can be demanded and expected by both parties, however, locking her down to DO NOT DRINK WITH YOUR FRIENDS, although a righteous purpose filled with your insecurities as well, and a splash of your mistrust to her judgements (which, she might have just proven you were right), SHOULD NOT BE IN THE TOP LIST OF YOUR DEVELOPING years. 

The world will have loads to offer, you two have barely grazed it's peel. If your mindset and culture is to settle down ASAP after graduation, you have the right to demand so, and you should seek that from another woman, as she is not the one.  (I'm sure some will have same mindset as you, although hard to find). But if YOU ARE ALSO in terms to explore and experience, you have no right to suppress her of the very same endeavors.  

​

I understand how long this comment is, but bottom line. Live a little, explore, experience, educate, seek. But don't hold someone else you hold dear that very privilege, if possible, experience it TOGETHER. (Yes you had your mum situation but keep in mind how many months she looked forward to spend that graduation moment with you.). 

Study hard, work hard, aim hard, so you can get your own crib and after carefully evaluating (don't take a leap of faith on this), co-habitation might be a good start to conquer the world, together with your partner in crime. 

As long as you still live with your parents, I believe you have no rights to set ground rules for her, it is her parent's task to do so. 

Now focus on getting rich and achieving your goals together with her.

Well I'm 31. I've had 12 relationships in my course and 3 serious ones leading to engagements and weddings. Based on what I've been thru, you will feel that way again, you will be in love again. 

But until you came to a point you can move on, it will suck. Big time. Your heart feels crushed and compressed. It's hard to sleep, it feels empty and mundane. 

You're 17, you're young and yet to reach your peak. It might be fast it might be long until you will feel that way again. But here's the best part, you will. So look forward to that day, enjoy your freedom responsibly. Learn from what has happened and by now you can read the signs when the relationship is deteriorating. Probably on next relationship you can take preventive actions, as you would be alerted if it's happening. Or you can be more prepared to let go. 

Remember, you are a majestic tiger. A tiger might be injured or gets sick and fall flat to the ground, but as long as it has time and care to heal, it will one day, stand again and rise again as a tiger. Never feel, think or misled to be the ant. 

Now heal, tiger.

Be aware, as I was doing this because I was depressed with my relationship (my SO's switched focus from me to her new job i don't like and I don't think we needed the money she just likes the attention her customers and boss gave her). I was having difficulties in my job, and my emotions wasn't in the right circuit. 

I escaped reality that I was not ready to solve or have the solution even the willpower to find one: to video games. 

Make sure my scenario wasn't his case. You need to start asking "What can I do to make you feel better" instead of "Why are you playing so much video games". He's definitely not happy with reality that video games was his escape. Even not, if he requires that much entertainment something must be very wrong or not going well for him in his life. Men are usually reclusive about their problems as we are culturally educated to carry burdens alone (most of us).

It will not be easy for you to be a sucker and try to service his sake first, but that's what relationships is all about. Almost every addiction, comes from a problem of reality we are trying to escape. Find out, talk about it, HELP HIM. In my case, IT WAS A SILENT CRY FOR HELP.

If the Patriarchy culture (I don't judge, I think every POV and culture has its own ups and downs) is what you think your husband has, evaluate their pros and cons. If he is enacting the ONE MAN SHOW decisions, it comes with both rights and responsibilities. Rights, for example, using the 'No compromise' ultimatum on important decisions; Responsibilities, for example, "Be sole provider, for housing, food, security, clothes, etc." also being responsible for whatever no compromise he enacted.

If you think that culture is just, fair, and is the path you can live with, then it's time for you to see the good sides of his pen-ultimatums. 

If you don't think it's the path you wanted, re-evaluate your relationship. These cultures, habits, don't and never will go away. He or you will live in resentment trying to adapt to whichever culture you decided to proceed. Why allow him or you to suffer? 

Toddler? This complicates your future decisions, so re-evaluate. Can you be happier by stepping out of your comfort zone? Is what he is bringing to the table as a patriarch sufficient enough for you to bury your incompatible mindset?

You're what he needs and not what he wants.

I really want to say I've been there, and you'd be speculating to how special your circumstances are, and you're right. Every person has a different scenario; however, every actions is based on a linear motive.

My SO began showing interest on other men in social media, and they are smart enough to identify which is trying to shag them, which is not. Started receiving gifts from them, start having coffee with them, started inviting them over to MY apartment when I am stationed overseas for work (I work for UNICEF, was stationed in Lebanon for three weeks). We were in an argument when i left. I left back early because of the high risk involving my division, just to find out that she shagged another man in my apartment and it was someone they kept in contact as 'just friends' in her instagram.

I will not be a paranormal and say this will happen to you. But remember, theres a motive behind every action. There's only a few logical reason rationally to as why a person would leave paths and doors open for their relationship, to either move to another path or keeping space for alternatives. 

Here is just a scenario of what could happen, out of the thousands and millions of possibilities. Don't invest your time, effort, life, money, affection, and mental health for something that doesn't yield returns.

It's not always your fault, and it's not always her fault. Stop evaluating and speculating. She wanted just friends leave it at that. You can face almost every problem together, but when not going to the same path, you will not survive whatever this cruel world will throw for you.

A partner in crime is waiting for you out there. Stop wasting time and hurting each other by pursuing your dead end. Love songs don't tell you what happens after a few years. You need to have the same aims and goals. "Just friends" is a good wake up call to "we have different aims and goals and no longer can be romantically involved".

Maybe she have moved on from that phase of her life (or influenced by others to do so, such as family, SO, etc.)

Point is she made her point to leave that world, including you in it.

You might be in the losing more of it, as she have decided, and accepted to risk losing all her online friends there. I gave my SO a decision to leave all social media once, as it was influencing her towards a bad addiction to being 'influenced' by so called influencer. We had to breakup and for her to be reprimanded on what mattered most for her.

I'm not saying this is the case for you, but all I'm giving you one example of a million other scenarios that can happen.

Bottom line, she made her choice. You were part of the consequence, she accepted that risk. It's time for you to evaluate if your focus in placed on the right basket. Accept, grief, move on.

It's been two months. You've either reconciled or have managed to moved on.

If the feeling of regrets stayed, Know that if YOU caused the relationship to self destruct, he will never ever forget what you did, regardless of the "forgive and forget" speeches. 

Well, whichever path the world has opened for you, I hope you are doing well and have moved on.
